---
name: loci
description: Agent-owned codebase navigation infrastructure. Use when repository work needs source retrieval or relationship tracing. For standalone documentation or configuration checks where symbol navigation is irrelevant, use a targeted direct read. Skip retrieval only when relevant source from the target checkout is already observed, current, and sufficient.
---

# loci — codebase retrieval

Use Loci's normal MCP operation for repository source discovery and relationship
tracing. Supply the actual repository root and the question or known identity.
Loci selects graph context deterministically inside the operation.

## Inspect evidence before acting

A filename, recalled summary or startup index count is not source inspection.
Skip retrieval only when the relevant source from the target checkout is already
observed, current and sufficient for this action. Refresh affected evidence after
edits. Exact edits require the full affected source, including relevant callers
when the change depends on them.

## Normal workflow

First locate the normal entrypoints by their exact operation names. With
`tool_search`, search for `loci_retrieve` and `loci_read`. In Code Mode, use
this names-only discovery pass:

```javascript
const matches = ALL_TOOLS.filter(t => /(?:^|__)loci_(?:retrieve|read)$/.test(t.name));
store("loci.normal.tools", matches);
text({
  status: matches.length ? "found" : "no_match",
  count: matches.length,
  names: matches.slice(0, 8).map(t => t.name)
});
```

Then exact-match the selected name and read its complete live description and
input declaration before invoking it. Discovery returns names only; full
descriptions belong to that second, single-tool pass. A zero-match result
requires the setup check below; it does not establish missing configuration.

```text
loci_retrieve(repo, query="the source or behavior needed")
loci_retrieve(repo, query="src/known-file.ts")
loci_retrieve(repo, seed_ids=[known_id], query="remaining source question")
loci_read(repo, source_ref=returned_item.source_ref)
```

Use `loci_retrieve` for initial discovery and further context. It creates or
refreshes the index and runs the maintained graph policy. The response includes
candidate identities, selected source, proved relationships, coverage and
omissions. Read the returned source and proof before deciding it is sufficient.
Several candidates remain alternatives; an omitted match is not disproved.

For an incomplete source item, pass its short `source_ref` unchanged to
`loci_read`. Follow `next_source_ref` until the exact source needed is complete.
A stale or unavailable reference requires fresh retrieval. Re-anchor a returned
node ID with `loci_retrieve` when further context is needed. Repeating an identical request
against an unchanged snapshot returns the same bounded selection.

Both operations take `repo`. Traversal families, direction, depth, ranking and
budgets are owned by Loci; there are no per-request policy controls. An import's
file/package/module endpoint remains distinct from its selected declarations.
The `ownership` field describes indexed source membership and is not a semantic
relationship. A zero-edge packet does not prove that no dependencies exist.

## Coverage and failures

Preserve partial/unknown coverage and unsupported, unresolved, ambiguous,
external, inaccessible, stale and budget omissions in conclusions. Stored edges
prove only the supported static relationship, not runtime dispatch or exhaustive
impact. Rust `declared_possible` configuration remains possible.

Treat `structuredContent.error` as a failure with a code, message and details.
A busy catalog or refresh lock calls for a bounded retry after the writer can
finish; it does not authorize catalog repair. For repeated unchanged failures,
report the limitation and use a targeted source-read fallback where necessary.
Standalone documentation or configuration checks where symbol navigation is
irrelevant may use a targeted direct read.

## Setup and operator diagnostics

The normal MCP catalog contains `loci_retrieve` and `loci_read`. If focused
discovery cannot find them, read
[setup-and-cli.md](references/setup-and-cli.md) for local stdio setup, store
identity and the temporary fallback. An old loaded catalog can require a fresh
host session after installation. Report the actual visibility limitation.

Low-level search, outline, get, explore and graph utilities belong to an
operator-selected diagnostic server. Changing the surface is an installation
choice, not ordinary retrieval routing. When explicitly investigating Loci
itself through that surface, consult
[graph-navigation.md](references/graph-navigation.md) and
[tool-contracts.md](references/tool-contracts.md).

Read [normal-retrieval.md](references/normal-retrieval.md) when interpreting the
normal packet, exact-source continuation or work limits. Read
[language-resolution.md](references/language-resolution.md) when a particular
language's static resolution guarantee or omission affects the task.
Resolve a file-symlinked `SKILL.md` to its real source path before following
relative references.

# Normal retrieval results

`loci_retrieve(repo, query="", seed_ids=None)` is the normal source operation.
At least one query or exact node ID is required. A query equal to an indexed
relative path selects that file. Otherwise symbol metadata is ranked, with
bounded literal-source matching when metadata yields no anchor. Several
candidates are alternatives, not unique resolution.

A case-sensitive camel/Pascal-case or underscore identifier in a question gives
an identically named code declaration priority over prose matches. Duplicate
declarations remain alternatives. Plain-language document questions keep the
metadata ranking; this is not arbitrary-name or runtime symbol resolution.

The `normal-graph-v1` policy always inspects supported calls, types, value
references and imports in both directions. It traverses up to two semantic
hops, interleaves relationship families and returns source with proved edges.
Direct relationships of selected anchors precede ownership expansion. Shared
declarations connected to two selected anchors by supported type edges receive
priority over incidental calls; only those type edges get this priority.
For each selected callable, indexed parameter annotations prioritize one
representative input-type path, including a supported contract dependency within
the two-hop limit. Other branches retain normal family interleaving.
Return types and body calls do not establish parameter roles. A nested generic
type argument whose input/return role is absent from the index receives no
inferred input priority.
Every delivered edge still requires its complete static proof.
The same snapshot and request produce the same selection. The live schema
publishes the fixed work, source and complete-result limits.

Read these fields together:

- `anchors` identifies the starting candidates; `selection` reports matching
  scope and candidate omissions.
- `nodes` holds exact identities; `items` carries selected source and whether
  the whole owning extent is present. Use an item's `source_ref` for expansion.
- `relationships` retains the native edge direction, traversal direction,
  resolution qualification and IDs of its complete proof source.
- `ownership` connects declarations to their indexed file/package/module/crate
  context. It is separate from semantic relationships.
- `sources` holds exact byte/line spans and hashes. A preview can be exact bytes
  while still being an incomplete declaration; inspect `items.complete`.
- `scope`, `status` and `omissions` bound conclusions. Partial results may still
  contain useful evidence; no result is exhaustive runtime impact.
- `usage` distinguishes examined nodes, considered/traversed edges, delivered
  relationships, unique source bytes and the complete MCP-result bytes.

`loci_read(repo, source_ref)` pages one hash-bound source extent. Pass the short
returned handle unchanged; `next_source_ref` continues that extent and
`complete=true` ends it. Loci retains the exact repository, path, content hash
and byte extent in the configured per-repository cache. Handles survive server
restarts while that bounded cache retains them. An unknown or evicted handle
requires fresh retrieval; changed source returns `SOURCE_STALE` instead of
applying old offsets. Legacy encoded locators remain readable for compatibility.
References locate source; they are not authorization credentials or proof that
an earlier caller received the source. A read discovers no other source.

Re-anchor a returned identity to request further graph context under the same
policy. This is a new bounded retrieval, not a guarantee to enumerate omitted
neighbors. Use operator diagnostics for an explicit investigation of graph
storage, resolver records or index health.

# Anvil Repo Guidance

## Instruction Priority

Follow current system, developer, and user instructions first. Treat this file as project guidance, not a substitute for explicit user direction.

Continuity is not truth. Current user instruction, current files, command output, tests, and live project evidence override stale continuity.

## Production Quality

Anvil optimizes for the right production-grade result, not the smallest diff,
minimum viable implementation, or quickest first slice.

- Treat correctness, durability, recovery, security, observability, migration
  discipline, operability, and proportionate verification as part of the
  implementation when the capability depends on them. They are not optional
  polish to defer until after dogfooding.
- Accept complexity when the production requirements earn it. Prefer simpler
  designs only when they satisfy those requirements completely.
- Use incremental tasks and commits to keep work reviewable and recoverable.
  Incremental delivery sequences a production-grade design; it does not
  authorize temporary-grade foundations or knowingly incomplete safety.
- Keep product scope bounded. Do not add speculative features, unrelated
  abstractions, or drive-by cleanup under the banner of production quality.
- If the approved architecture or plan would force an underbuilt result, stop
  and correct the architecture or plan before implementation.

## Manifest V2 Delivery Invariant

Before planning, designing, implementing, reviewing, or resuming Manifest V2,
read
`docs/manifest-rings/manifest-v2-delivery-invariant.md`. Apply its
language calibration and complexity gate to every slice, and point back to it
in the active plan or handoff. For Manifest, “production-grade” is bounded by
the accepted graph-based, Git-backed, one-primary-session operating model.
The active Implementation-phase authority is
`docs/plans/2026-09-03-manifest-v2-corrected-implementation-plan.md`;
the original definition, 2026-09-01 plan, and ADR-017 Decision body are
historical inputs rather than executable instructions.

## Plan Readability

For new or meaningfully revised active plans and specifications:

- End every major `##` section with one plain-language blockquote in the form
  `> **TL;DR:** <one succinct sentence>`.
- Make the summary useful on its own in the context of the document: name the
  subject and state the concrete meaning, decision, or consequence. If the
  section introduces the thing being built, explain what it is and what it
  does rather than merely saying to build or deliver it.
- Do not merely restate the heading, list unexplained internal terms, or hide
  the section behind phrases such as "deliver the substrate". Do not introduce
  new requirements, evidence, or caveats in the TL;DR.
- Let nested `###` sections roll into their parent summary. Give standalone
  checkpoints their own TL;DR because they are independent review gates.
- Keep the detailed section authoritative for the document's design contract.
  The TL;DR is a compression aid, not a second contract; current user
  instructions and live evidence govern active work state.
- Apply a deletion test: if the detailed section disappeared, its TL;DR should
  still give Vik a useful plain-language understanding of what that section
  contributed, even though it cannot preserve every detail.
- Do not bulk-rewrite historical plans merely to apply this convention. Add it
  when a plan is active or otherwise being meaningfully revised.

## Completion Handoffs

Treat every substantive engineering completion update as a user-facing release
gate. Open in ordinary language and answer, in this order:

1. **What now works** that did not work before.
2. **Why it matters** to the actual goal Vik is pursuing.
3. **What remains or happens next**, including any important boundary on what
   was completed.

Technical evidence comes after that explanation. Do not lead with changed
files, commit hashes, test counts, schema names, internal phase labels, or a
technical changelog and expect Vik to reconstruct the result.

Apply a rejection test before sending: if the opening would require Vik to
translate repository vocabulary or implementation details to understand what
was achieved, the handoff must be rewritten before sending.

## Anvil Continuity Tool Use

Use Anvil continuity as calibrated workspace memory, not as a mandatory every-turn ritual.

- Read continuity when orientation matters, the current frame is uncertain, or a session/work boundary needs recovery.
- When accepted work must survive a conversation boundary, use `anvil_continuity_checkpoint_task` to set or replace the singular active task, mark it waiting, or clear it when no work remains. Supply a retry-stable checkpoint id, update the checkpoint whenever the task or next step changes, and verify the returned rendered frame before ending the turn.
- Use `anvil_continuity_record_event`, `anvil_continuity_promote_event`, and `anvil_continuity_retire_projection_item` for durable signals outside the active task. The repo CLI is acceptable for continuity `read`, `doctor`, and `init-default`, but not as the discovery path for mutation. If the required MCP mutation tool is unavailable, stop and report the missing MCP surface instead of probing or inventing a CLI mutation path.
- Work Context binding ids and mutation routing are supplied by the host adapter. Do not invent a binding id, reuse one from another session, or pass a repository path to make it the Continuity owner.
- Record a continuity event when durable non-task signal emerges: an approved decision, open question, correction, phase change, repeated failure mode, or capability change.
- Promote a recorded event only when it should appear in the compact injected frame for future sessions.
- Treat the compact injected frame as the current working set. If promotion fails because a projection list is full, retire the least-current compact item with a correction event, then promote the current signal. Prefer evicting historical implementation notes before active decisions, current next actions, accepted working examples, or live open questions. Retiring a projection item must not delete event history.
- Keep the compact frame fresh proactively. Follow the Anvil MCP continuity tool instructions for hygiene triggers and the maintenance loop; this repo guidance records that compact-frame freshness is required even before the tool is called.
- Do not record routine command output, transient failed attempts, raw conversation dumps, vague impressions, one-off mood signals, secrets, or current file facts that should be re-inspected.
- Ask or make the write explicit before recording stable profile changes, project identity constraints, sensitive information, public-facing commitments, memory corrections that rewrite stable memory, or stable capability promotion.
- Treat `.anvil/` continuity as orientation state. Durable repo decisions and process rules still belong in tracked docs, ADRs, plans, code, tests, or git history as appropriate.

## Skill Invocation Journal

Use the skill invocation journal as local operational evidence for whether skills are triggering correctly.

- Log when a skill is used, when a skill was missed and noticed later, or when a skill fired incorrectly.
- Record concise trigger summaries, not full raw prompts or sensitive content.
- Always provide an explicit outcome and concrete reason. `used` means the
  skill changed the work through a specific action; `missed` means it should
  have fired but did not; `false_positive` means it fired but did not
  contribute. Loading a skill and then finding it irrelevant is
  `false_positive`, not `used`.
- Bound MCP logging attaches trusted host/session trace automatically, and the
  Codex hook adds turn/message ids when the host supplies them. CLI logging
  requires explicit host and session ids.
- Keep this out of continuity unless the pattern itself becomes a durable decision, repeated failure mode, next action, or capability change.
- For agent-driven logging and bounded reads, use the Anvil MCP tools
  `anvil_skill_invocation_log`, `anvil_skill_invocation_read`, and
  `anvil_skill_invocation_audit_sample`. The CLI remains available for operator
  inspection and as a fallback when the ambient MCP surface is unavailable.
- Before any skill-doctrine review, and approximately every 50 new traceable
  records while evidence collection is active, request a reproducible sample
  of 10 records. Have a fresh-context reviewer compare the recorded outcome
  and reason with the linked turn where available. Record discovered misses or
  false positives as new incident rows that cite the original invocation id;
  do not rewrite journal history.

Commands:

```bash
node bin/anvil.ts skills log --skill <name> --trigger <summary> --outcome <used|missed|false_positive> --reason <summary> --host <host> --session-id <id> [--turn-id <id>] [--message-id <id>]
node bin/anvil.ts skills invocations [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>] [--skill <name>] [--outcome <used|missed|false_positive>] [--session-id <id>] [--json]
node bin/anvil.ts skills audit-sample --seed <label> [--size <n>] [--skill <name>] [--outcome <used|missed|false_positive>] [--session-id <id>] [--json]
```

Skill invocation records are workspace-local under `.anvil/skill-invocations/` and must not be committed.

## Brain Usage Journal

Use the Brain usage journal as local operational evidence for how Brain is being used and where it may be stale, wrong, blocked, or underused.

- Log concise usage events by default; use `--prompt-raw` only when raw triggering prompt evidence is intentionally useful. Do not log raw Brain excerpts, unrelated session dumps, or sensitive content.
- The unified `UserPromptSubmit` hook automatically records one objective recall event: `recalled`, `no_match`, `degraded`, or `disabled`. These events prove what the hook did, not whether the agent used or benefited from the result.
- For every Brain-adjacent task or turn, log exactly one coverage event: `consulted`, `used`, `not_needed`, or `blocked`.
- Add incident events only when they happen: `updated`, `missed_update`, `stale`, `wrong`, or `eval_failed`.
- Use severity `info`, `warn`, or `error` when the default `info` is not enough.
- Use `--pages` and `--related` for comma-separated page paths and event IDs when they help later inspection.
- Use trace fields when the triggering session/message is known: `--session-id`, `--turn-id`, `--message-id`, `--mcp-call-id`, `--prompt-excerpt`, and `--prompt-raw`. Use `--trigger-bucket` only when an explicit manual classification is better than the journal's deterministic auto-classification.
- Keep this out of continuity unless the pattern itself becomes a durable decision, repeated failure mode, next action, or capability change.
- Do not use this as automatic Brain ingestion. Brain updates remain part of agent judgment and steward maintenance.
- Treat coverage events as the denominator for later metrics. Do not skip `not_needed` just because Brain was not consulted.
- For agent-driven manual logging, bounded reads, and metrics, use the Anvil MCP tools `anvil_brain_usage_log`, `anvil_brain_usage_read`, and `anvil_brain_usage_metrics`. The log tool accepts manual coverage and incident outcomes only and intentionally excludes prompt content. Keep automatic recall collection on the unified prompt hook; do not reproduce it through MCP.
- Brain identity is system-owned. New records use the configured agent's stable `brain_id`; aliases are display metadata. The legacy `--brain` flag and MCP `brain` field are compatibility assertions only and fail when they do not match the configured Brain.

Commands:

```bash
node bin/anvil.ts brain log --event <recalled|no_match|degraded|disabled|consulted|used|not_needed|updated|missed_update|stale|wrong|blocked|eval_failed> --trigger <summary> [--brain <legacy-compatibility-assertion>] [--trigger-bucket <bucket>] [--session-id <id>] [--turn-id <id>] [--message-id <id>] [--mcp-call-id <id>] [--prompt-excerpt <text>] [--prompt-raw <text>] [--pages <comma-list>] [--related <comma-list>] [--outcome <summary>] [--severity info|warn|error]
node bin/anvil.ts brain usage [--limit <n>] [--json]
node bin/anvil.ts brain metrics [--json]
node bin/anvil.ts brain dashboard [--host <host>] [--port <port>] [--refresh-ms <n>] [--json]
brain dashboard
```

# Normal retrieval results

`loci_retrieve(repo, query="", seed_ids=None)` is the normal source operation.
At least one query or exact node ID is required. A query equal to an indexed
relative path selects that file. Otherwise symbol metadata is ranked, with
bounded literal-source matching when metadata yields no anchor. Several
candidates are alternatives, not unique resolution.

A case-sensitive camel/Pascal-case or underscore identifier in a question gives
an identically named code declaration priority over prose matches. Duplicate
declarations remain alternatives. Plain-language document questions keep the
metadata ranking; this is not arbitrary-name or runtime symbol resolution.

The `normal-graph-v1` policy always inspects supported calls, types, value
references and imports in both directions. It traverses up to two semantic
hops, interleaves relationship families and returns source with proved edges.
Direct relationships of selected anchors precede ownership expansion. Shared
declarations connected to two selected anchors by supported type edges receive
priority over incidental calls; only those type edges get this priority.
For each selected callable, indexed parameter annotations prioritize one
representative input-type path, including a supported contract dependency within
the two-hop limit. Other branches retain normal family interleaving.
Return types and body calls do not establish parameter roles. A nested generic
type argument whose input/return role is absent from the index receives no
inferred input priority.
Every delivered edge still requires its complete static proof.
The same snapshot and request produce the same selection. The live schema
publishes the fixed work, source and complete-result limits.

Read these fields together:

- `anchors` identifies the starting candidates; `selection` reports matching
  scope and candidate omissions.
- `nodes` holds exact identities; `items` carries selected source and whether
  the whole owning extent is present. Use an item's `source_ref` for expansion.
- `relationships` retains the native edge direction, traversal direction,
  resolution qualification and IDs of its complete proof source.
- `ownership` connects declarations to their indexed file/package/module/crate
  context. It is separate from semantic relationships.
- `sources` holds exact byte/line spans and hashes. A preview can be exact bytes
  while still being an incomplete declaration; inspect `items.complete`.
- `scope`, `status` and `omissions` bound conclusions. Partial results may still
  contain useful evidence; no result is exhaustive runtime impact.
- `usage` distinguishes examined nodes, considered/traversed edges, delivered
  relationships, unique source bytes and the complete MCP-result bytes.

`loci_read(repo, source_ref)` pages one hash-bound source extent. Pass the short
returned handle unchanged; `next_source_ref` continues that extent and
`complete=true` ends it. Loci retains the exact repository, path, content hash
and byte extent in the configured per-repository cache. Handles survive server
restarts while that bounded cache retains them. An unknown or evicted handle
requires fresh retrieval; changed source returns `SOURCE_STALE` instead of
applying old offsets. Legacy encoded locators remain readable for compatibility.
References locate source; they are not authorization credentials or proof that
an earlier caller received the source. A read discovers no other source.

Re-anchor a returned identity to request further graph context under the same
policy. This is a new bounded retrieval, not a guarantee to enumerate omitted
neighbors. Use operator diagnostics for an explicit investigation of graph
storage, resolver records or index health.
